title: AI Agent Security Policy - Tier-2 Coding Agents

scope.governs: Tier-2 AI coding agents: any LLM-based system that can propose or apply changes to application source code, pipelines, or infrastructure-as-code in Olympus-controlled environments.
scope.excludes: Tier-1 agents (documentation summarization, test generation without write access)

requirements.detail: All tools exposed to a Tier-2 agent must go through the gateway registry.
The minimum OAuth/API scope needed, per tool, never account-level credentials.
Tools not on the allowlist are unreachable; a denied call returns AUTHZ_DENIED and must be logged.
Maximum TTL 900 seconds; renewal requires a new capability grant.
Direct shell access is prohibited. Shell-equivalent tools (file write outside the repo sandbox, network calls beyond the package registry allowlist) are Tier-3 and require two-person approval.

layers_in_order.detail: Schema-validate every tool call against the registry entry; reject unknown parameters.
Filesystem restricted to the workspace; outbound network restricted to allowlisted domains.
Diff review plus secret scan before any merge. An agent change that introduces a new dependency must include an SCA report with a maximum CVSS of 7.0 for known vulnerabilities.

compensating_controls: agent output quarantined to a fork
no direct writes to protected branches
full prompt-and-response transcript retained for 30 days
when_teams_move_faster_than_policy.unregistered_exception_treated_as: policy violation, not a technicality, escalated to the CISO office

rules: All AUTHZ_DENIED events are reviewed weekly by AppSec; three denials for the same tool in one week trigger a registry review.
The gateway registry itself is version-controlled; changes require a pull request with AppSec approval.
Quarterly red-team exercise must include at least one prompt-injection attempt against a Tier-2 agent.
